analysis_steps.goal: Derive Sigma_star and Sigma_SFR from MaNGA Pipe3D

method.value: Use Pipe3D spaxel stellar mass and extinction-corrected Halpha (Balmer decrement) converted to SFR, with spaxel area and inclination correction

evidence.quote: we utilize the spaxel-based stellar mass and SFR measurements from `Pipe3D`, taking into account the physical area of the spaxel and applying an inclination correction.
The extinction-corrected H$\alpha$ luminosity is converted to the SFR using the calibration provided by (cite: Ken98).
The correction is based on a Milky Way extinction curve with a standard reddening parameter $R_{V}$ of 3.1 (cite: Car89).
A Salpeter initial mass function (cite: Sal55) is assumed in this work.
$H_\mathrm{0}$ = 70 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_\mathrm{m}$ = 0.3, and $\Omega_\mathrm{\Lambda}$ = 0.7.

analysis_steps.goal: Classify spaxels and assign Sigma_sSFR for non-star-forming and quenched spaxels

method.value: BPT plus Halpha EW cuts define star-forming, AGN-contaminated, retired and fully-quenched spaxels; for non-star-forming spaxels with D4000 < 1.45 Sigma_sSFR is read from the median Sigma_sSFR-D4000 relation built from star-forming spaxels of the 34 non-starburst galaxies, then multiplied by Sigma_star; fully-quenched spaxels fixed at log(Sigma_sSFR/yr^-1) = -12

evidence.quote: We first construct the $\Sigma_\mathrm{sSFR}$-D4000 relation for our sample using star-forming spaxels from the 34 non-starburst star forming galaxies.
Then, we convert the $\Sigma_\mathrm{sSFR}$ to $\Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}$ by multiplying it with the $\Sigma_{\ast}$ value of these spaxels.
the fully-quenched spaxels are artificially assigned to a fixed value of log($\Sigma_\mathrm{sSFR}$/yr$^{-1}$) $=$ $-$12

claims.hypothesis: Radial profiles of star formation and molecular gas properties change systematically with distance from the star-forming main sequence

claims.finding: Quenching is global with an inside-out signature, and both f_gas and SFE are suppressed

evidence.quote: The radial profiles of $\Sigma_\mathrm{sSFR}$, $f_\mathrm{gas}$, and SFE consistently exhibit a gradual decrease in magnitude from the SF$_{h}$ group to the SF$_{l}$ group across almost all radii.

evidence.loc: Relative Importance of $f_\mathrm{gas}$ and SFE in Individual Galaxies
